case_title: Dhirendra Kumar @ Dhiroo v. State of Uttarakhand
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity arising from an earlier altercation over an alleged night-time knocking at a household member's door
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW 3, PW 4); medical (post-mortem by PW 6); motive evidence (PW 7); corroborating witness (PW 2)
aggravating_circumstances: Multiple head and face wounds with pulverized bones; injuries inflicted with full force on the head; prior enmity; cruel manner
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Criminal appeal dismissed; conviction under s.302 and life sentence upheld
neutral_facts: On the evening of 1 April 1983, the victim was struck with a stone at about 8.30 pm in a village. About four days earlier, during a festival, the victim had visited the accused's home. Later that night the accused came to the victim's household to assault the victim, alleging that the victim's family had been involved in an incident of knocking at the door of a woman in the accused's household at night with evil intention. Family members intervened, preventing the accused from dragging the victim out, and the accused left with a threat. The victim did not return home that night. The next morning a witness said he had seen the victim with the accused at about 7.30 pm, and two eyewitnesses said they saw the accused beating the victim with a stone at about 8.30 pm. Another witness said he had seen the two together just before the incident. The victim's body was later found near a riverbank. The post-mortem recorded that the face and head were flattened, with multiple irregular lacerated wounds, a disfigured face, pulverized skull and mandible bones, and brain matter flowing from the wounds. The death was attributed to shock and haemorrhage from ante-mortem injuries which could have been caused by a stone between 8 and 9 pm. The accused was examined and had three injuries to the face, which the doctor said were caused by a hard blunt object or friction about a day earlier. The accused said he had been falsely implicated because of complaints he had made against local officials.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from shock and haemorrhage due to multiple head and face injuries; accused had three minor facial injuries
motive: Prior enmity from the earlier incident (alleged night-time knocking at a household member's door), accepted by the court as furnishing motive
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness evidence of PW 3 and PW 4; PW 7's evidence on the earlier incident; PW 2's evidence of the accused and deceased together before the occurrence; nature of injuries on the deceased
witness_credibility: Both courts below found PW 3 and PW 4 reliable; PW 7 believed on motive; defence version found unreliable
trial_duration: offence: 1 April 1983; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 17.11.2007; Supreme Court: 26 February 2015
legal_representation: Appellant: Hema Sahu, Rajendra Sahu, C. L. Sahu; Respondent (State): Jatinder Kumar Bhatia
investigation_status: FIR lodged 2 April 1983; investigation completed by SO; post-mortem conducted; accused sent up for trial
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
defence_argument: Eyewitnesses unreliable; motive far-fetched; case covered by Exception 4 to s.300 (sudden fight), so s.304 Part II applies
legal_principle_applied: Article 136 interference only for patent illegality or perversity; burden on accused to prove sudden fight under Exception 4; case-by-case s.302 vs s.304 factors
precedent_relied_upon: Ankush Shivaji Gaikwad vs. State of Maharashtra, 2013 (6) SCC 770 (cited by the appellant; distinguished; its factor test applied)
sentencing_rationale: No separate sentencing rationale; the court found previous enmity and fatal injury to a vital part with full force, not a sudden fight, and saw no ground to interfere
judicial_aggravating_factors: Previous enmity; fatal injuries to a vital part with full force; cruel manner; no sudden provocation or heat of passion
